idiom_name: enum with associated values + exhaustive switch
implementation_notes: Swift's enum with associated values is the closed set (enum Shape { case circle(r: Double), rect(w: Double, h: Double) }), and switch over it must be exhaustive: omitting a case is a compile error, so no default arm is needed and none is wanted - each operation is one switch with pattern-bound payloads, which replaces the visitor/double-dispatch structure entirely. indirect covers recursive cases, and @unknown default is the deliberate escape for non-frozen library enums, where the compiler warns if the default arm also matches a case that is now known. Keep the protocol-plus-classes form when the set must be extended by other modules; Swift protocols cannot be switched exhaustively.
pitfalls: A default (or case _) arm silences exhaustiveness for every future case; in a non-frozen library enum use @unknown default instead, which warns when it shadows a case that has become known.
Recursive enums need indirect (or an indirect case) or the payload is stored inline and recursive values do not compile.
A switch compiled against a newer library enum can still trap at run time, so recompiling consumers is part of the closure contract.
